briefFidelity: FAIL — and this is the gate. Writing blind I reached for 'totemic figure', 'lashed effigy', 'bundle of splints', 'spine'. Not one botanical word occurred to me: no leaf, frond, stem, plant, or growth. The brief's two explicit formal instructions are the two things absent. (1) 'Fine linework throughout, delicate rather than heavy... the drawing carried in line rather than in mass' — blind, I described the unit as 'straight quadrilateral bars with squared ends', 'chunky chevrons', 'overlapping flat-ended bars'. The dominant mark is a wide semi-transparent slab; 9906's members read as planks. That is mass, and the majority of the twelve are built from it. Only 10443, 10980 and 9727 are actually linear. (2) 'A stem that divides, and divides again, each division smaller and turned slightly from the last' — no recursion is legible anywhere. 9011, 9369 and 10264 do have a spine with lateral elements, which is a partial first-order read, but the laterals are same-scale slabs rather than progressively smaller, slightly rotated sub-divisions, and 10801 is seven identical chevrons stacked with no diminution at all. Four tokens (9906 starburst, 10085 horizontal striation, 10622 C-arc, 10443 crossing scribble) have no stem to divide from. The palette instruction — moss and bone on a dark ground — is met exactly, and the generous emptiness is met. But palette is the easiest clause in the brief and it is the only one carried cleanly.
seedVariation: Varied, but varied along the wrong axis. The brief asks for one form at different extents of growth; what is here is several unrelated organising schemes — a radial starburst, a stack of horizontal striations, a swept arc, a chevron column, a crossing scribble — held together only by palette and stroke shape. They are not one work at twelve rotations, so it clears that failure, but they are also not twelve stages of one growth: they read as different systems sharing a colourway. And one of the twelve, 9190, renders nothing at all in every size and every market condition. A blank cell is not 'growth that has not gone far'; it is an empty token, and this is a permanent on-chain commitment.
thumbnailSurvival: Partial. The strong tokens hold their silhouettes at 120px — starburst, striation stack, C-arc and chevron column are each individually identifiable, and the spined figures keep their shape. But three of twelve are effectively blank at browse size: 9727 is a few hairlines that nearly vanish against the black, 9548 is a smudge, and 9190 is nothing. A collection page with a quarter of its cells reading as empty does not survive browsing, and the chevron detail that carries most of the character dissolves into generic texture.
marketResponse: Visible, directionally sensible, but not the claimed transformation. Stress strips strokes and drains the light values toward grey; recovery adds the most strokes and returns the brightest whites. That reads at browse size on the larger tokens. What the brief claimed, though, is that recovery 'extends the branching and multiplies its divisions' and stress 'retracts the form back toward a bare armature'. What actually happens is density and lightness modulation — there is no branch structure to extend, so nothing subdivides further in recovery, and 9548 under stress does not expose an armature, it disintegrates into two disconnected bars. The mechanism is a weight change dressed as a growth change.
tokenIdentity: Mixed. 9011 and 9369 hold their skeleton across all three conditions and are unmistakably the same object. 9548 does not — stress reduces it to two horizontal bars and a fragment that nobody would match to its neutral state. 9190 is absent in all three, which is a degenerate pass rather than a real one.
composition: No clipping and no severe mush; the dense tokens (9011, 10264) soften slightly where many semi-transparent slabs overlap, but they hold. Focal hierarchy is weak — most tokens are an undifferentiated tangle with no apex, no growing tip, no clear point of origin, which is precisely the hierarchy a frond would supply. Frame use is loose to a fault: nearly everything is centred with a wide black margin and little bleeds to an edge, and the scale variance is uncontrolled rather than expressive — 9906 fills the canvas while 9548 and 9727 occupy under a tenth of it and 9190 occupies none.
reasoning: Blind, I described a set of ritual objects — effigies and bundles of splints lashed around a spine — built from heavy overlapping slabs, in moss and bone on black, that get denser and brighter or sparser and greyer with market condition. The brief asked for a botanical abstraction carried in fine line rather than mass, whose structure is a stem dividing and dividing again with each division smaller and slightly turned, and whose market response is the extension and multiplication of that branching. The palette clause lands perfectly and the emptiness clause lands, but the two clauses that would make the thing a frond — linear rather than massive, recursive rather than scattered — are the two that are missing, and their absence is why my unprompted reading went to effigy rather than to plant. The market response is real and visible but is a density swing, not the multiplication of divisions it is claimed to be, because there are no divisions to multiply. On top of the brief failure, one of twelve holdout tokens renders as an empty frame in every condition and two more are near-empty at browse size. Any one of those would warrant refusal before an irreversible commitment; together they are not close.
wouldChange: Make the form an actual recursive branching rule and let everything else follow from it: a stem that spawns children, each child shorter than its parent by a fixed ratio and rotated a few degrees from it, recursing to a depth that is itself the growth parameter. That single change is what supplies the botanical read, gives 'how far the growth has gone' a real axis across seeds, gives recovery something to genuinely subdivide and stress a bare armature to retract to, and makes fine linework the natural mark — a branch is a line, and the current thick slab is a symptom of there being no branch to draw. It would also eliminate the empty token, since a depth-1 recursion still draws a stem.
